Augustin Bizimungu is arrested for his involvement in the Rwandan genocide.
President Hugo Chávez of Venezuela is restored to power following an attempted coup.
Romanian mathematician Preda Mihăilescu creates a proof for the Catalan's conjecture, which had gone unsolved for 158 years.
South African Mark Shuttleworth blasts off from the Baikonur Cosmodrome on the Soyuz TM-34, becoming the first African space tourist.
Erfurt school massacre: An expelled student kills 16 people and commits suicide at a school in Erfurt, Germany.

Bojayá massacre: A church is struck with a cylinder bomb during a conflict between the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia and the United Self-Defense Forces of Colombia, killing an estimated 119 people.
NASA launches the Aqua satellite as part of the Earth Observing System.
2002 Kaspiysk bombing: Over 40 people are killed when insurgents bomb a military parade in Kaspiysk, Russia.
American FBI agent Robert Hanssen is sentenced to life in prison for espionage.
Rebels bombard Arthington, Liberia, with artillery during the Second Liberian Civil War causing panic in the neighboring capital, Monrovia.
Kaluchak massacre: Militants attack a bus and an Indian army camp in Kaluchak, Jammu and Kashmir, killing 31 people and escalating the India-Pakistan standoff.

Timor-Leste independence: East Timor regains its independence as the Democratic Republic of Timor-Leste after 2.5 years of United Nations administration and 26 years of Indonesian occupation since 1975.
Nepali Prime Minister Sher Bahadur Deuba asks King Gyanendra to dissolve the parliament amid escalation of the Nepalese Civil War.
United States President George W. Bush and Russian President Vladimir Putin sign the Strategic Offensive Reductions Treaty.
The NATO-Russia Council is established.

The formal eight-month rescue and recovery operation at Ground Zero in New York City officially concluded with a solemn, largely silent ceremony, marking the completion of the removal of approximately 1.8 million tons of debris from the site following the September 11 attacks.
The 2002 FIFA World Cup begins, taking place in South Korea and Japan.
The Kyoto Protocol is ratified by the European Union.
Archaeologists begin uncovering the Liye Qin Slips in Liye, China.
The ringed dwarf planet Quaoar is discovered by astronomers Chad Trujillo and Michael Brown at the Palomar Observatory.
The Zeyzoun Dam in Zayzun, Syria, fails.
The Lennox Lewis vs. Mike Tyson boxing fight takes place. Following a scuffle prior to the match, Lennox Lewis defeats Mike Tyson.
British scientist Kevin Warwick carries out first direct electronic communication experiment between the nervous systems of two humans.
The ImClone stock trading case begins when ImClone Systems CEO Samuel D. Waksal is arrested for insider trading.
Afghanistan changes its official longform name to the Transitional Islamic State of Afghanistan.
The United States withdraws from the Anti-Ballistic Missile Treaty with Russia.
Russia withdraws from the START II nuclear reduction agreement with the United States.
2002 Bou'in-Zahra earthquake: A 6.5 magnitude earthquake strikes north-western Iran, killing over 200 people.
The WorldCom scandal breaks and the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission begins its investigation into WorldCom.

Second Battle of Yeonpyeong: During the 2002 FIFA World Cup in South Korea and Japan, two North Korean patrol boats cross a contested border in between the two Koreas and attack two South Korean Chamsuri-class patrol boats.

2002 FIFA World Cup: Brazil beats Germany 2-0 in the 2002 FIFA World Cup Final with Ronaldo scoring the two goals; Brazil's captain Cafu, who becomes the first player to appear in three successive World Cup finals, accepts the trophy on behalf of the team.
The Rome Statute comes into force, thereby establishing the International Criminal Court.
NASA launches the CONTOUR satellite but loses contact.
The Imperial War Museum North opens in Trafford, England.
The Organisation of African Unity is disbanded and replaced by the African Union.
The Church of England allows divorcees to remarry.
The first synthetic virus is announced after being successfully created and tested at Stony Brook University.
Former Argentine junta leader Leopoldo Galtieri is arrested for the kidnap, torture, and murder of 20 leftist guerillas during the Dirty War.
The discovery of the early hominid Sahelanthropus is announced.
Militants attack in Qasim Nagar, Jammu and Kashmir, killing 29 people.
The only captive baiji dolphin dies as the species approaches extinction.
The Machakos Protocol is signed during the Second Sudanese Civil War, establishing a framework for peace talks and possible independence of South Sudan.
At the height of the WorldCom scandal, WorldCom files the largest bankruptcy in American history.
Salvadoran generals José Guillermo García and Carlos Eugenio Vides Casanova are found liable for torture in an American court.
August 4 - The 2002 Commonwealth Games are held in Manchester, England.
The Sknyliv air show disaster takes place, killing 77, becoming the deadliest air show accident of all time.
The AKS primality test is published by Manindra Agrawal, Neeraj Kayal, and Nitin Saxena from the Indian Institutes of Technology.
2002 Khankala Mi-26 crash: Chechen separatists shoot down a Russian Mil Mi-26, killing 127 soldiers. It was the worst aviation disaster in the history of the Russian military.
September 4 - Typhoon Rusa, the most powerful typhoon to hit South Korea in 43 years, makes landfall, killing at least 236 people.
September 4 - Earth Summit 2002 takes places in Johannesburg, South Africa, aimed at discussing sustainable development by the United Nations.
EUMETSAT launches the Meteosat 8 satellite as part of its Meteosat program.
Switzerland joins the United Nations as the 190th member state after rejecting a place in 1986.
Yemeni al-Qaeda operative Ramzi bin al-Shibh is arrested in Pakistan for involvement in the September 11, 2001 attacks. He will later be found unfit to stand trial.
27 - Hurricane Isidore crosses Cuba, the Yucatán Peninsula, and Louisiana.
General Robert Guéï leads an army mutiny in an attempt to overthrow Ivory Coast President Laurent Gbagbo, resulting in civil war.
October 4 - Hurricane Lili crosses Cuba and several other Caribbean islands before making landfall in Louisiana.

The Senegalese ferry MV Le Joola sinks off the West African coast with 1,863 people killed according to official reports, making it one of the worst peacetime maritime disasters in history. Only 64 passengers survive.
East Timor is admitted to the United Nations as the 191st member state; it also changes its official longform name from "Democratic Republic of East Timor" to "Democratic Republic of Timor-Leste".
Operation Enduring Freedom - Horn of Africa: The United States deploys troops to the Horn of Africa to combat Islamist groups and pirates.
Former Republika Srpska president Biljana Plavšić pleads guilty to crimes against humanity for her involvement in the Bosnian genocide.
The genome sequences for malaria carriers anopheles gambiae and plasmodium falciparum are published.
The International Court of Justice rules in favor of Cameroon in Cameroon v. Nigeria.
The United States Congress approves military action in Iraq should it fail to comply with United Nations requirements for weapons of mass destruction.
Jemaah Islamiyah militants detonate multiple bombs in two nightclubs in Kuta, Bali, killing 202 people and injuring over 300 people, making it the worst terrorist act in Indonesia's history.
The Somali Reconciliation Conference begins, initiating peace talks between two factions of the Somali Civil War: the Transitional National Government and the government of Puntland.
The Indian military stands down from the border with Pakistan, ending the standoff between the two nations.
The Bibliotheca Alexandrina opens in Alexandria, Egypt, in a ceremony attended by several heads of state.
The European Space Agency launches the INTEGRAL observatory.
The discovery of the James Ossuary is announced.
26 - Chechen rebels take control of the Nord-Ost theatre in Moscow and hold the audience hostage. At least 170 people are killed following a Russian attempt to subdue the militants.
2002 Bahraini general election: Bahrain holds its first Parliamentary elections since 1973.
The culprits of the D.C. sniper attacks are arrested after they kill ten people in the United States over the previous three weeks.
2002 Brazilian general election: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva is elected President of Brazil.
Belarus restricts religious activity outside of the Belarusian Orthodox Church with a new law.
2002 Denali earthquake: A 7.9 magnitude earthquake, one of the strongest North American earthquakes recorded, occurs in Alaska.
A sovereignty referendum is held in Gibraltar. The people reject Spanish sovereignty.
The United Nations Security Council unanimously adopts Resolution 1441, forcing Iraq to either disarm or face "serious consequences". Iraq agrees to the terms of the resolution on November 13.

Prestige oil spill: Greek oil tanker MV Prestige begins spilling oil off the coast of Galicia. It will continue until November 19, spilling 60,000 tonnes of oil in the worst environmental disaster in the history of the Iberian Peninsula.
Hu Jintao becomes General Secretary of the Chinese Communist Party.
2002-2004 SARS outbreak: The first case of the Severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARS) epidemic, a zoonosis caused by a coronavirus, is recorded in Guangdong province of south China.
Prague summit: NATO announces seven new countries that intend to join: Bulgaria, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Romania, Slovakia, and Slovenia.
The Hague Code of Conduct is signed to regulate intercontinental ballistic missiles internationally.

U.S. President George W. Bush signs the Homeland Security Act into law, establishing the Department of Homeland Security, in the largest U.S. government reorganization since the creation of the Department of Defense in 1947. Following a several month-long transitional period, it commences operations

2002 Mombasa attacks: Suicide bombers blow up an Israeli-owned hotel in Mombasa, Kenya, but their colleagues fail in their attempt to bring down an Arkia Israel Airlines charter flight with surface-to-air-missiles.
Opponents of President Chavez begin a strike in Venezuela.
The government of Burundi signs a ceasefire with the CNDD-FDD rebel group to end the Burundian Civil War. It holds until February 2003.
A peace agreement is made in the Second Congo War, approving the creation of the Transitional Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
The International Court of Justice rules in favor of Malaysia in the Ligitan and Sipadan dispute with Indonesia.
2002 Grozny truck bombing: Chechen suicide bombers attack the government headquarters in Grozny, Russia, killing over 70 people.
2002 Kenyan general election: Kenya holds its first free elections, ousting the dominant Kenya African National Union Party following a victory of the National Rainbow Coalition.
Shenzhou 4 is launched from China.
The United Nations Mission in Bosnia and Herzegovina ends.
Tel Aviv central bus station: Two Palestinian suicide bombers attack a neighborhood in Tel Aviv, killing at least 23 people and injuring 103.
The discovery of OGLE-TR-56b, the first exoplanet to be discovered through transit photometry, is announced.
North Korea announces its withdrawal from the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons.
The last signal from NASA's Pioneer 10 spacecraft is received, some 12.2 billion kilometers (7.6 billion mi) from Earth.
NASA loses contact with the Pioneer 10 probe after nearly 31 years.
The 1492 painting Descent into Limbo by Andrea Mantegna sells for $28.6 million.
Waterfall rail accident: An Intercity Tangara G set train derails near Waterfall, killing 7 and injuring 40 others. The cause was of a faulty deadman's brake.
At the conclusion of the STS-107 mission, the Space Shuttle Columbia disintegrates during reentry over Texas, killing all seven astronauts on board.

The Federal Republic of Yugoslavia is renamed to "Serbia and Montenegro" (after its two constituent states) after its leaders reconstitute the country into a loose state-union between Montenegro and Serbia, marking an end to the 73-year-long use of the name "Yugoslavia" by a sovereign state.

U.S. Secretary of State Colin Powell gives a speech to the United Nations presenting the case for a military invasion of Iraq. It will later be discovered that the United States Bush administration misled him when preparing his testimony.
North Korea announces that it has resumed its nuclear weapons program.
The 2003 Cricket World Cup begins. It is held in South Africa, Zimbabwe, and Kenya, and it ends on March 23 with Australia defeating India in the final.
The first set of data from the Wilkinson Microwave Anisotropy Probe is published.
Dolly the sheep, the clone of a mammal, dies.
Millions of people worldwide take part in massive anti-war protests in anticipation of the United States and its allies invading Iraq to overthrow Saddam Hussein's regime.
The Station nightclub fire: A fire broke out at a music venue in West Warwick, Rhode Island, United States, killing 100 people and injuring 230.
2003 Bachu earthquake: A 6.8 Mwearthquake strikes in Xinjiang, killing 257 people.
The War in Darfur begins after rebel groups rise up against the Sudanese government.

Former Bosnian Serb leader Biljana Plavšić is sentenced by the United Nations International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia to 11 years in prison for war crimes committed during the Bosnian War.
Rowan Williams becomes Archbishop of Canterbury.
Khalid Sheikh Mohammed of al-Qaeda is captured in Rawalpindi, Pakistan.
SCO Group files a lawsuit against IBM as part of an ongoing dispute regarding the use of Unix in the development of Linux.
Peace talks break down in the First Ivorian Civil War.
Malta approves joining the European Union in a referendum.
The International Criminal Court begins operations.
The first test of the GBU-43/B MOAB bomb takes place.
Prime Minister Zoran Đinđić of Serbia is assassinated in Belgrade by a sniper.
The World Health Organization issues a global alert on SARS when it spreads to Hong Kong and Vietnam after originating in Mainland China.
Former General François Bozizé seizes power through a military coup in the Central African Republic.
U.S. President George W. Bush presents a 48-hour ultimatum for Iraqi president Saddam Hussein to resign.
Invasion of Iraq begins
2003 Nadimarg massacre: Islamist militants gather and execute citizens of a Hindu village in Kashmir, killing 24 of the 54 residents.
Slovenia approves joining the European Union and NATO in a referendum.
In its first military operation, the European Union takes over peacekeeping operations in Macedonia from NATO's Operation Allied Harmony.
The Archaeological Survey of India orders that Hindus be allowed to worship in the Kamal Maula Mosque.
U.S. forces seize control of Baghdad, ending the rule of Saddam Hussein.
Hungary approves joining the European Union in a referendum.
Five college students are murdered in an unsolved arson in Columbus, Ohio.
The Human Genome Project is completed, with 99% of the human genome sequenced to 99.99% accuracy.

The Treaty of Accession is signed in Athens between the European Union and ten countries (Czech Republic, Estonia, Cyprus, Latvia, Lithuania, Hungary, Malta, Poland, Slovenia and Slovakia), concerning these countries' accession into the EU, leading to the 2004 enlargement of the European Union.
Indian Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee visits Kashmir and expresses support for peace negotiations with Pakistan.
Tropical Storm Ana becomes the first recorded North Atlantic tropical storm to occur in April.
The North Korean ship Pong Su is seized by the Royal Australian Navy for smuggling heroin into the country.
The Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam break away from peace talks in the Sri Lankan Civil War.
The iTunes Store launches.
2003 Bingöl earthquake: A 6.4 Mw earthquake strikes in Bingöl, Turkey, killing 177 people.
U.S. President George W. Bush declares an end to the invasion of Iraq in the Mission Accomplished speech. Hostilities would continue for several years during a period of Iraqi insurgency.
A ceasefire takes effect in the First Ivorian Civil War.
John Paul II visits Umayyad Mosque in Damascus, becoming the first pope ever to enter a mosque.
2003 Sri Lanka cyclone: A cyclone makes landfall in Sri Lanka, killing 260 people and causing the country's worst natural disaster in 50 years.
Lithuania approves joining the European Union in a referendum.
2003 Znamenskoye suicide bombing: Chechen suicide bombers attack a government office in Znamenskoye, Russia, killing at least 59 people.
Contact with infected prairie dogs causes the first outbreak of human mpox in the Western Hemisphere. Cases continue until June 11.
Slovakia approves joining the European Union in a referendum.
Peace talks break down in the insurgency in Aceh and the Indonesian government launches new attacks against the insurgents.
2003 Boumerdès earthquake: a 6.8 Mw earthquake strikes in Algeria, killing over 2,200 people.
The World Health Organization adopts its first treaty, the WHO Framework Convention on Tobacco Control.
The Eurovision Song Contest 2003 takes place in Riga, Latvia, and is won by Turkish entrant Sertab Erener with the song "Everyway That I Can".
A Boeing 727 aircraft is stolen from an airport in Luanda, Angola triggering an international terrorist investigation by the FBI and CIA. The aircraft and its pilots were never found.
Georges Rutaganda becomes the first person to be convicted of war crimes by the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda, and his previous charges are upheld.
Prometea, the world's first cloned horse, is born.
Opposition figures and peace activists, including Aung San Suu Kyi, are arrested in Myanmar.
The United Nations authorizes peacekeeping operations in the Ituri Province of the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
The Strategic Offensive Reductions Treaty comes into effect between Russia and the United States.
Mars Express launches, containing the Beagle 2 lander.
An agreement is reached for the United Nations to form a Khmer Rouge Tribunal.
Poland approves joining the European Union in a referendum.
NASA launches the Spirit rover.
The opening of a thousand-year-old coffin is broadcast live on Chinese television.
Homo sapiens idaltu is proposed as a new human subspecies based on the Herto Man fossils.
The Czech Republic approves joining the European Union in a referendum.
The 50th Venice Biennale begins.
Operation Desert Scorpion: U.S. forces in Iraq facilitate searches for Ba'athist forces, distribution of humanitarian aid, and engineering programs to repair damaged infrastructure.
Former President of France Valéry Giscard d'Estaing presents his draft for a Constitution of the European Union.
Declaration of Thessaloniki: The European Union encourages accession of states of the western Balkans.
Lennox Lewis vs. Vitali Klitschko: Boxer Lennox Lewis defends his title as heavyweight boxing champion against Vitali Klitschko.
The release of the novel Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix becomes a worldwide cultural event and boosts the literary industry.
Warring parties in the Democratic Republic of the Congo sign a peace accord, bringing an end to the Second Congo War.
The annual 1 July Marches in Hong Kong see hundreds of thousands of participants in response to the National Security (Legislative Provisions) Bill.
The Migrant Workers Convention comes into effect.
In a major development in football, English footballer David Beckham is transferred from Manchester United F.C. to Real Madrid CF for £17.25 million.
August - 2003 European heat wave: Europe experiences its hottest summer in over five centuries.
SARS is declared to be contained by the World Health Organization.
NASA launches the Opportunity rover.
The Three Gorges Dam in China begins operating when the first of its 34 generators is activated.
The existence of PSR B1620−26 b, the oldest known exoplanet in the galaxy, is confirmed using observations from the Hubble Space Telescope.
The Iraqi Governing Council is created by the United States as an ethnically diverse provisional government of Iraq.
The United Self-Defense Forces of Colombia agrees to disband.
Major Fernando Pereira leads a failed coup against President Fradique de Menezes in São Tomé and Príncipe.
The government of the Philippines signs a ceasefire with the Moro Islamic Liberation Front. It takes effect the next day.
The Convention on the Future of Europe finishes its work and proposes the first European Constitution.
The Regional Assistance Mission to the Solomon Islands, led by Australia, begins after ethnic violence engulfs the island country.
The Tasman Spirit oil spill occurs in Pakistan.
The final Volkswagen Beetle is produced.
Milomir Stakić receives the first life sentence issued by the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia.
The Second Liberian Civil War ends after President Charles Taylor resigns and flees the country.
Riduan Isamuddin, head of the Indonesian Islamist group Jemaah Islamiyah, is arrested in Ayutthaya, Thailand.
NATO takes over command of the peacekeeping force in Afghanistan, marking its first major operation outside Europe in its 54-year-history.
The discovery of the dinosaur species Rajasaurus narmadensis is announced.

An overloaded power grid following the failure of FirstEnergy's alarm system in their control room causes the Northeast blackout of 2003, affecting more than 50 million people in the United States and Canada with nearly 100 related deaths.
Libya formally accepts civil responsibility for the bombing of Pan Am Flight 103 in 1988.
Element 110 is formally named darmstadtium by the International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry.
Peace talks between Maoist rebels and the Nepalese government are interrupted by resumed hostilities in the Nepalese Civil War.
A peace agreement is reached to formally end the Second Liberian Civil War.
Shmuel HaNavi bus bombing: A Palestinian suicide bomber kills at least 18 people in a bus bombing in Jerusalem.
In the Canal Hotel bombing in Baghdad, 22 people are killed, among them United Nations' Special Representative in Iraq Sérgio Vieira de Mello.
The G21 (later called the G20 developing nations) forms in response to disputes around the upcoming World Trade Organization Ministerial Conference of 2003.
The Brazilian VLS-1 launcher explodes on the launchpad on August 22, killing 21 people.
The Spitzer Space Telescope is launched from Cape Canaveral, Florida.

Car bombs explode at Gateway of India and Zaveri Bazaar in Mumbai, claiming 54 lives and injuring 244 others. Pakistan-based Lashkar-e-Taiba is blamed for the attack. The attack causes an escalation in the Kashmir conflict.
Mars makes its closest approach to Earth in over 60,000 years.

The first six-party talks, involving South and North Korea, the United States, China, Japan and Russia, convene to find a peaceful resolution to the security concerns of the North Korean nuclear weapons program.
Imam Ali mosque bombing: A bomb kills at least 125 people, including Mohammad Baqir al-Hakim, at a Shia mosque in Najaf, Iraq.
Typhoon Dujuan makes landfall in Guangdong as a category 1 typhoon with sustained winds of 90 mph.
Hurricane Fabian strikes Bermuda.
Armenia abolishes capital punishment entirely, following a law on August 1 that abolished it in most cases.
Al-Qaeda leaders Osama bin Laden and Ayman al-Zawahiri release their first video statement since 2001.
The four-day World Trade Organization Ministerial Conference of 2003 begins in Cancún.
Swedish foreign minister Anna Lindh is murdered.
The Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety comes into effect.
Cambodia and Nepal are approved for membership in the World Trade Organization.
Typhoon Maemi, makes landfall in South Korea as a category 3 typhoon with sustained winds of 125 mph.
General Veríssimo Correia Seabra leads a bloodless coup against President Kumba Ialá in Guinea-Bissau. He steps down to create a new civilian government days later.
Estonia approves joining the European Union in a referendum.
Sweden rejects joining the Eurozone in a referendum.
Hurricane Isabel makes landfall in North Carolina.
The United Nations establishes the United Nations Mission in Liberia with Resolution 1509.
Latvia approves joining the European Union in a referendum.

October 12 - The 2003 FIFA Women's World Cup is held in the United States after the tournament is moved from China due to the SARS outbreak. Germany win their first title after they defeated Sweden in the final with a golden goal.
NASA ends the Galileo probe mission after nearly 14 years by sending it into Jupiter's atmosphere.
The ceasefire in the First Ivorian Civil War breaks down.
AMD releases the Athlon 64, the first 64-bit processor to be released for consumer use.
The Hubble Space Telescope starts the Hubble Ultra-Deep Field, making 800 exposures, until January 16, 2004.
Two parties in the Second Sudanese Civil War, the National Islamic Front and the Sudan People's Liberation Movement, reach a peace agreement.
The 8.3 Mw Tokachi earthquake occurs off the coast of Hokkaido.
SMART-1, an ESA spaceprobe and ESA's first mission to the moon, is launched from Kourou, French Guiana.
The United Nations Convention Against Transnational Organized Crime comes into force.
Hurricane Kate first reaches hurricane status.
Maxim restaurant suicide bombing: A Palestinian suicide bomber attacks a restaurant in Haifa, Israel, killing at least 19 people.
Israeli warplanes strike alleged Islamic jihad bases inside Syrian territory, the first Israeli attack on the country since the 1973 Yom Kippur War.
Hezbollah and the Israel Defense Forces engage in hostilities in the Shebaa Farms.
Nokia releases a handheld game console, the N-Gage. It becomes a major critical failure in the gaming industry.
November 22 - The 2003 Rugby World Cup is held in Australia and is won by England who defeated Australia in the final after extra time.
Gyude Bryant becomes President of Liberia as a compromise choice after former President Charles Taylor fled the country during the Second Liberian Civil War.
China launches Shenzhou 5, the country's first human spaceflight.
The United Nations Security Council adopts Resolution 1511 to approve American-led governance in Iraq.
Pope John Paul II holds mass to celebrate his 25th anniversary as pope, becoming the fourth pope to reach the milestone.
Argentine General Antonio Domingo Bussi is detained for crimes committed in the Dirty War.
Mother Teresa is beatified by Pope John Paul II.
After acknowledging that it has produced enriched uranium, Iran agrees to suspend its nuclear program.
The Aarhus Protocol on Persistent Organic Pollutants comes into effect.
A Russian air base opens in Kant, Kyrgyzstan, as Russia's first foreign air base since the dissolution of the Soviet Union.
Concorde makes its last commercial flight, bringing the era of airliner supersonic travel to an end.
27 October 2003 Baghdad bombings: A series of car bombings occur in Baghdad, Iraq, targeting multiple police stations and a Red Cross headquarters. Approximately 40 people are killed.
Russian businessman Mikhail Khodorkovsky is arrested. Critics allege that this is a political action by the government to control Russian oligarchs.
The International Court of Justice rules in the Oil Platforms case that the United States was not justified in its 1987 attacks on Iranian oil platforms but that neither party violated a 1955 treaty.
The dwarf planet Sedna is discovered by a team of astronomers led by Michael E. Brown from the Palomar Observatory.

Suicide bombings occur in Istanbul. Further attacks occur five days later. They kill 63 people between them, making them the two deadliest terror attacks in Turkey, and cause uncertainty in the international economy.

Baghdad DHL attempted shootdown incident: Shortly after takeoff, a DHL Express cargo plane is struck on the left wing by a surface-to-air missile fired by the Islamic Army in Iraq and forced to land. All three crew members survive without injuries.
A ceasefire is reached at the Line of Control in Kashmir.
The supersonic passenger jet, Concorde, makes its last ever flight from Heathrow Airport in London to Bristol Filton Airport.
Trial of Stanislav Galić: The International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia sentences Stanislav Galić to 20 years in prison for crimes against humanity.
The United Nations Convention Against Corruption is opened for signing.
Saddam Hussein, the former president of Iraq, is captured in the small town of Ad-Dawr by the U.S. Army.
The Beagle 2 Mars lander deploys, but contact is lost.
Libya agrees to eliminate all of its materials, equipment, and programs aimed at producing weapons of mass destruction.
The 6.6 Mw Bam earthquake occurs in Iran.
The Protocol on Heavy Metals comes into effect.
An insurgency breaks out in southern Thailand.
NASA's Spirit rover lands on the surface of Mars.
The RMS Queen Mary 2, at the time the largest ocean liner ever built, is christened by its namesake's granddaughter, Queen Elizabeth II.
Bartholomew I of Constantinople visits Cuba.
NASA's Opportunity rover lands on the surface of Mars.
Two suicide bombings are carried out by al-Qaeda in Erbil, the capital of Iraqi Kurdistan.
Janet Jackson suffers a wardrobe malfunction during the halftime show of Super Bowl XXXVIII.
The Rotterdam Convention comes into force.
Haitian president Jean-Bertrand Aristide is overthrown in a coup d'état.
The European Space Agency launches the Rosetta space probe.
A series of bombings occur in Karbala, Iraq, killing over 140 Shia Muslims commemorating the Day of Ashura.
NASA releases the Hubble Ultra-Deep Field image of early galaxies.
Al-Qaeda bombings on Cercanías trains in Madrid, Spain, kill at least 192 people.
Vladimir Putin is reelected president of Russia with 71.2 percent of the vote.
Ethnic violence breaks out in Kosovo between Albanians and Serbs.
Hamas leader Ahmed Yassin is killed by Israeli missile strikes.

Bombings attributed to the Islamic Movement of Uzbekistan kill 15 in Tashkent, the capital of Uzbekistan. This is the first instance of suicide bombings in the country or the surrounding region of central Asia.
Bulgaria, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Romania, Slovakia and Slovenia are admitted to NATO, the largest expansion of the organization.
The International Court of Justice rules in the Avena case that the United States had violated its obligations to the Vienna Convention on Consular Relations when prosecuting Mexican nationals.
Four American security contractors are killed in Fallujah, Iraq, leading to the First Battle of Fallujah.
The Communist Party of Nepal (Maoist) abducts over 1,000 people from the Bajura District to fight in the Nepalese Civil War.
Google launches Gmail.
The Siege of Sadr City begins when the Mahdi Army ambushes American soldiers in Sadr City, Iraq.
The United Nations Operation in Côte d'Ivoire begins to maintain a ceasefire in the First Ivorian Civil War.
The Humanitarian Ceasefire Agreement is signed by the Sudanese government and two rebel groups to create a ceasefire in the War in Darfur.
A newborn western gorilla is observed for the first time in 50 years in the Léfini Faunal Reserve.
Poland bans the use of chlorofluorocarbons.
Israeli helicopters fire missiles at a convoy of vehicles in the Gaza Strip, killing Hamas leader Abdel Aziz al-Rantisi.
Newly elected prime minister of Spain, José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero, announces the withdrawal of all 1,300 Spanish troops from Iraq.
Russia launches the Soyuz TMA-4 mission.
Ukrainian boxer Vitali Klitschko becomes the WBC world heavyweight champion after defeating his opponent Corrie Sanders.
The Gherkin opens in London.
Patriarch Bartholomew I of Constantinople breaks Eucharistic communion with Archbishop Christodoulos of Athens.
The European Union expands by 10 new member states: Cyprus, the Czech Republic, Estonia, Hungary, Latvia, Lithuania, Malta, Poland, Slovakia, and Slovenia.
Garçon à la pipe, painted by Pablo Picasso in 1905, is sold for $104.2 million. This was the highest price a work of art had ever been sold for at auction.
The discovery of the post-perovskite form of magnesium silicate is reported.
Vladimir Putin is sworn in for a second term as Russia's president.
A stadium bombing in Grozny, Chechnya, Russia kills ten people, including regional governor Akhmad Kadyrov.
15 - The Eurovision Song Contest 2004 takes place in Istanbul, Turkey, and is won by Ukrainian entrant Ruslana with the song "Wild Dances".
The Ralito II Agreement is signed between Colombia and the United Self-Defense Forces of Colombia.
The Stockholm Convention on Persistent Organic Pollutants enters into force.
Manmohan Singh, a Sikh, is sworn in as India's first non-Hindu prime minister.
The Seattle Central Library opens in Seattle, Washington.
A fire at a Momart warehouse destroys numerous works of art.
The United Nations Stabilisation Mission in Haiti (MINUSTAH) peacekeeping mission begins in Haiti.
A transit of Venus occurs.
In Mojave, California, United States, SpaceShipOne becomes the first privately funded spaceplane to achieve spaceflight.
The International Criminal Court opens an investigation into crimes against humanity during the Second Congo War.
The US-led coalition occupying Iraq, the Coalition Provisional Authority (CPA), transfers sovereignty to the Iraqi Interim Government.
The International Treaty on Plant Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture enters into force.
Saddam Hussein appears in court for his charges to be read.
The Cassini-Huygens orbiter reaches the orbit of Saturn.
The International Court of Justice issues an advisory ruling that the construction of the West Bank barrier violates the Palestinian people's right to self-determination.
The use of magnetic resonance imaging to study the spin of a single electron is reported.
The Mexican government files charges against former President of Mexico Luis Echeverría for his role in the 1971 Corpus Christi massacre.
The International Criminal Court opens an investigation into the actions of the Lord's Resistance Army in Uganda.
The Frauenkirche church finishes reconstruction after its destruction in 1945.
NASA's MESSENGER space probe is launched, with its primary mission being the study of Mercury.
The Battle of Najaf begins in Najaf, Iraq.
Guangzhou Baiyun International Airport begins operation in Guangzhou, China.
13 - Typhoon Rananim causes widespread destruction as it strikes China.
Fighting breaks out in the Georgian-Ossetian conflict.
The Rio-Antirrio Bridge opens in Greece.
29 - The 2004 Summer Olympics are held in Athens, Greece.
Google makes its initial public offering.
Armed robbers steal Edvard Munch's The Scream, Madonna, and other paintings from the Munch Museum in Oslo, Norway.
Two Russian passenger jets are downed by suicide bombers during the Second Chechen War.
The immunity of former Chilean dictator Augusto Pinochet is revoked so he can be charged with crimes against humanity.
Former Yugoslavian president Slobodan Milošević stands trial for crimes against humanity.
Chechen rebels take 1,128 hostages, mostly children, at a school in Beslan, Russia. Russian security forces eventually storm the building, resulting in more than 330 people being killed.
A fire breaks out at the Duchess Anna Amalia Library.

In the AFL finals, Essendon defeated Melbourne by five points (15.14.104 - 15.9.99) in the elimination final at the Melbourne Cricket Ground. The victory would prove to be Essendon's most recent finals win, beginning a finals drought that would extend for more than two decades.
Fijian golfer Vijay Singh unseats Tiger Woods as the top PGA Tour player.
The Scottish Parliament Building opens.
The Genesis space probe crash-lands in Utah after a three-year study of the Sun.
An explosion in Ryanggang Province, North Korea, prompts suspicion that North Korea is testing nuclear weapons.
Patriarch Peter VII of Alexandria is killed in a helicopter crash.
Hurricane Jeanne hits the island of Hispaniola, killing thousands in the Dominican Republic and Haiti.
Israel launches a military offensive in the northern Gaza Strip.
Painkiller Vioxx is pulled from the market due to a potential doubling of heart attack risk.
Suicide bombers detonate two bombs at the Red Sea resort of Taba, Egypt, killing 34 people and injuring 171, mostly Israeli tourists.
Afghanistan holds its first presidential election. Hamid Karzai wins with 55.4 percent of the vote.
Russia launches the Soyuz TMA-5 mission.
The prehistoric human species Homo floresiensis is described.
Osama bin Laden releases a video taking credit for the September 11 attacks.
European heads of state sign in Rome the Treaty and Final Act, establishing the first European Constitution.
George W. Bush is reelected president of the United States, defeating his challenger John Kerry.
Conflict resumes in the First Ivorian Civil War as fighting breaks out between rebels and French peacekeepers.
Russia ratifies the Kyoto Protocol.
The Second Battle of Fallujah begins in Fallujah, Iraq.
Mozilla releases the Firefox browser.
Palestinian president Yasser Arafat dies. Mahmoud Abbas is appointed as his successor.
The European Space Agency probe SMART-1 arrives at the Moon, becoming the first European satellite to fly to the Moon and orbit it.
26 - Typhoon Muifa kills 600 people in the Philippines.
A ceasefire is reached between Uganda and the Lord's Resistance Army.
The SMART-1 satellite reaches the orbit of the Moon.
NASA launches the Swift Gamma-Ray Burst Explorer telescope.
The Museum of Modern Art reopens in its new location.
Nintendo releases the Nintendo DS handheld game console in North America.

The Orange Revolution begins, following a disputed presidential election in Ukraine where Viktor Yanukovych won against Viktor Yushchenko amid accusations of electoral fraud. A revote results in Yushchenko being declared the winner.
December 3 - Typhoon Nanmadol kills 775 people in the Philippines.
EUFOR takes over peacekeeping duties in Bosnia and Herzegovina from the United Nations.
The world's tallest bridge, the Millau Viaduct over the Tarn in the Massif Central mountains, France, is inaugurated.
Iraqi insurgents attack a U.S. military base in the city of Mosul, killing 22 people.

The 9.1-9.3 Mw Indian Ocean earthquake shakes northern Sumatra with a maximum Mercalli intensity of IX (Violent). One of the largest observed tsunamis follows, affecting coastal areas of Thailand, India, Sri Lanka, Somalia, the Maldives, Malaysia, Myanmar, Bangladesh, and Indonesia, killing 227,000
A peace agreement is reached between Senegal and the Movement of Democratic Forces of Casamance.
Jeanna Giese from Wisconsin, United States, comes home from the hospital and officially becomes the first person to ever survive rabies without a vaccination.
Eris, the most massive known dwarf planet in the Solar System, is discovered by a team led by Michael E. Brown using images originally taken on October 21, 2003, at the Palomar Observatory.
The Comprehensive Peace Agreement is signed, ending the Second Sudanese Civil War in Sudan.
Deep Impact is launched from Cape Canaveral with the purpose of studying the comet Tempel 1.
The Huygens spacecraft lands on Titan, the largest moon of Saturn.
The most intense solar particle event in recorded history is observed.
A presidential decree on redenomination of the Azerbaijani manat is issued, equating 1 new manat to 5000 old manats.
North Korea announces that it possesses nuclear weapons as a protection against the hostility it says it perceives from the United States.
YouTube, an American online video sharing and social media platform was founded by Steve Chen, Chad Hurley, and Jawed Karim headquartered in San Bruno, California.
Chad Hurley registers the youtube.com domain name.
Former Lebanese Prime Minister Rafic Hariri is assassinated, along with 21 others, by a suicide bomber in Beirut.
The Kyoto Protocol officially goes into effect.
2005 Liechtenstein general election: The Progressive Citizens' Party remains the largest party and wins a plurality of 12 seats in the Landtag.
China ratifies an anti-secession law, aimed at preventing Taiwan from declaring independence.

2008 financial crisis: U.S. President George W. Bush signs the revised Emergency Economic Stabilization Act into law, creating a 700 billion dollar Treasury fund to purchase failing bank assets.
A controversial Peruvian tape regarding a Norwegian oil company causes the 2008 Peru oil scandal, sparking protests which cause Jorge de Castillo to resign from office.
Microsoft announces the name Windows 7 to the public.
The Large Hadron Collider (LHC) is officially inaugurated at Geneva.
The Indian Space Research Organisation successfully launches the Chandrayaan-1 spacecraft on a lunar exploration mission.
Floods affected in Northern Vietnam and Central Vietnam and lasted 5 days causing flooding in many provinces and cities.
Satoshi Nakamoto publishes "Bitcoin: A Peer-to-Peer Electronic Cash System".

In a race won by Brazilian driver Felipe Massa, British driver Lewis Hamilton ends in 5th place in 2008 Brazilian Grand Prix and becomes the first black driver to win the Formula One World Championship, and the second youngest driver to achieve the feat at the age of 23.

2008 United States presidential election: Democratic U.S. Senator Barack Obama defeats Republican candidate John McCain and is elected the 44th President of the United States, making him the first African-American to be elected to the office.
Claudia Castillo of Spain becomes the first person to have a successful trachea transplant using a tissue-engineered organ.
The Buzzard Coulee meteorite falls in Saskatchewan. Reported to be 5 times brighter than the full moon and is seen in Alberta, Manitoba, and even North Dakota.

29 - 2008 Mumbai attacks: Ten terrorists of the Lashkar-e-Taiba, a Pakistan-based terror group, carry out four days of coordinated bombing and shooting attacks across Mumbai, killing 166 people. One terrorist, Ajmal Kasab, was captured alive and executed in 2012.
XL Airways Germany Flight 888T. An Airbus A320 due to be redelivered to Air New Zealand stalls and crashes over Mediterranean Sea resulting the deaths of 7
İzmir Wildlife Park has opened.
The police shooting of 15-year-old Alexandros Grigoropulos lead to riots across Greece.
The Channel Island of Sark, a British Crown dependency, holds its first fully democratic elections under a new constitutional arrangement, becoming the last European territory to abolish feudalism.
Bernard Madoff is arrested for securities fraud after he was turned in by his sons for operating the largest Ponzi scheme in history, later known as the Madoff investment scandal.

The International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda finds Théoneste Bagosora and two other senior Rwandan army officers guilty of genocide, crimes against humanity and war crimes and sentences them to life imprisonment for their role in the Rwandan genocide.

An ash dike ruptured at a solid waste containment area for a Tennessee Valley Authority coal-fired power plant in Roane County, Tennessee, releasing 4.2 million m (1.1 billion US gal) of coal fly ash slurry in the largest industrial spill in U.S. history.
A military coup d'état deposes the government of Guinea shortly after the death of longtime President Lansana Conté.
Israel invades the Gaza Strip, in response to rockets being fired into Israeli territory by Hamas, and due to weapons being smuggled into the area.
An extra leap second (23:59:60) is added to end of the year. The last time this occurred was in 2005.
European Certification and Qualification Association is founded.
National Disaster Recovery Fund, a disaster management fund is established by the Government of Jamaica.
Japan, Mexico, Turkey and Uganda assume their seats on the United Nations Security Council.
Asunción, the capital of Paraguay, becomes the American Capital of Culture and Vilnius and Linz become the European Capitals of Culture.
Slovakia adopts the euro as its national currency, replacing the Slovak koruna.

A Bay Area Rapid Transit police officer shoots and kills Oscar Grant, an unarmed black man, at Fruitvale station in Oakland, United States. The event becomes one of the inciting incidents for the global Black Lives Matter movement.
The first ("Genesis") block of the blockchain of the cryptocurrency and decentralized payment system Bitcoin is established by the creator of the system, known as Satoshi Nakamoto.
US Airways Flight 1549 ditches in the Hudson River in an accident that becomes known as the "Miracle on the Hudson", as all 155 people on board are rescued.
Gaza War: Hamas announces that they will accept the Israel Defense Forces offer of a ceasefire, ending the conflict.
Barack Obama is sworn in as the 44th President of the United States, becoming the first African-American to hold the office.
Virginia Tech student Zhu Haiyang decapitates Yang Xin in the first campus murder since the Virginia Tech shooting in 2007.
Israel withdraws from the Gaza Strip, officially ending its three-week war with Hamas. However, intermittent air strikes by both sides continue in the following weeks.
The first trial at the International Criminal Court opens. Former Union of Congolese Patriots leader Thomas Lubanga Dyilo is accused of training child soldiers to kill, pillage and rape.
The Icelandic government and banking system collapse. Prime Minister Geir Haarde immediately resigns.
An annular solar eclipse takes place over the Indian Ocean, the 50th solar eclipse of Saros cycle 131.
WikiLeaks releases 86 intercepted telephone recordings of politicians and businessmen involved in the 2008 Peru oil scandal.
Tiféret Israel Synagogue attack, profanation of the oldest synagogue in Caracas, Venezuela.
Jóhanna Sigurðardóttir is appointed as the new Prime Minister of Iceland, becoming the world's first openly lesbian head of government.
Patriarch Kirill of Moscow is enthroned as the Patriarch of the Russian Orthodox Church following the death of his predecessor, Alexy II in 2008.
Bushfires in Victoria leave 173 dead in the worst natural disaster in Australia's history.
2009 Liechtenstein general election: The Patriotic Union led by Klaus Tschütscher wins a majority of 13 seats in the Landtag.

Colgan Air Flight 3407 crashes in Clarence Center, New York while on final approach to Buffalo Niagara International Airport, killing all 49 people on board the aircraft as well as one person on the ground.

At 23:31:30 UTC, the decimal representation of Unix time reached 1234567890 seconds. Celebrations were held around the world, among various technical subcultures, to celebrate the 1234567890th second.

Soldiers of Bangladeshi border security force Bangladesh Rifles (BDR) mutiny and take the commanding army officers and their families hostages at the force's headquarters in Pilkhana, Dhaka. 57 army officers are killed along with 17 civilians by the mutineers.
Former Serbian president Milan Milutinović is acquitted by the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia regarding war crimes during the Kosovo War.
The President of Guinea-Bissau, João Bernardo Vieira, is assassinated during an armed attack on his residence in Bissau.

The International Criminal Court issues an arrest warrant for Sudanese President Omar al-Bashir for war crimes and crimes against humanity in Darfur. al-Bashir is the first sitting head of state to be indicted by the ICC since its establishment in 2002.

Michael Jackson announces his This Is It concert residency in London, England. However, a fortnight before the concerts were supposed to begin, Jackson died at the age of 50 from acute propofol intoxication.
NASA's Kepler Mission, a space photometer that will search for extrasolar planets in the Milky Way galaxy, is launched from Cape Canaveral Air Force Station, Florida, USA.
The President of Madagascar, Marc Ravalomanana, is overthrown in a coup d'état, following a month of unrest in Antananarivo.
A McDonnell Douglas MD-11 operated by FedEx suffers a bounced landing at Narita international airport resulting in the loss of 2 lives.
Rachel Crandall Crocker founds the International Transgender Day of Visibility.
Albania and Croatia join NATO.

North Korea launches a rocket from its Tonghae Satellite Launching Ground, which it says is carrying the Kwangmyŏngsŏng-2 satellite, prompting an emergency meeting of the United Nations Security Council.
A 6.3 magnitude earthquake strikes near L'Aquila, Italy, killing 308 and injuring more than 1,500.
April 2009 Moldovan parliamentary election protests: four people died and 270 were injured.
April 12 - Maersk Alabama Hijacking occurs, the ship being taken over by Somalian pirates off the coast of Somalia.
UNESCO launches The World Digital Library.
24 - Space Shuttle Atlantis is launched to refurbish the Hubble Space Telescope on May 11, landing at Edwards Air Force Base May 24.
16 - The Eurovision Song Contest 2009 takes place in Moscow, Russia, and is won by Norwegian entrant Alexander Rybak with the song "Fairytale".
The album 21st Century Breakdown is released by American rock band Green Day, which sold over 5 million copies.
France-Pakistan Atomic Energy Framework bilateral energy treaty is signed.
Video game Minecraft, the best-selling video game of all time, is first released to the public.
Following more than 25 years of fighting, the Sri Lankan Civil War ends with the total military defeat of the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam.
German football club RB Leipzig is founded by Red Bull.
North Korea announces that it has conducted a second successful nuclear test in North Hamgyong Province. The United Nations Security Council condemns the reported test.

"June 2009" redirects here. For the album by Toro Y Moi, see June 2009 (album). June 1 - Air France Flight 447, en route from Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, to Paris, crashes into the Atlantic Ocean, killing all 228 on board.
At&t Stadium opens to the public home of the NFL Dallas Cowboys
The outbreak of the H1N1 influenza strain, commonly referred to as "swine flu", is deemed a global pandemic.
Analog television ends in the United States as part of the digital television transition.

Mass protests erupt across Iran following a disputed presidential election in which Mahmoud Ahmadinejad was reelected president, the largest demonstrations in the country since the Iranian Revolution.
NASA launches the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter / LCROSS probes to the Moon, the first American lunar mission since Lunar Prospector in 1998.
War in Afghanistan: British forces began Operation Panther's Claw, in which more than 350 troops made an aerial assault on Taliban positions in southern Afghanistan.
Greenland gains self-rule.

June 2009 Washington Metro train collision, 9 people were killed and 80 people were injured when a Red Line (Washington Metro) train rear ended another train between Takoma and Fort Totten stations, this resulted in the worst train crash in DC Metro's history.

The death of American pop star Michael Jackson triggers an outpouring of worldwide grief. Online, reactions to the event cripple several major websites and services, as the abundance of people accessing the web addresses pushes internet traffic to unprecedented and historic levels.
The Military of Honduras ousts Honduran President Manuel Zelaya in a coup d'état, condemned by OAS.
Viareggio train derailment occurred when a freight train carrying liquified petroleum gas derailed at Viareggio railway station in Lucca, Italy. The accident killed 32 people and injured 26 people.
Yemenia Flight 626 crashes off the coast of Moroni, Comoros, killing all but one of the 153 passengers and crew.
Steve McNair, former NFL quarterback for the Tennessee Titans, is shot and killed by his girlfriend in Nashville, Tennessee.

Violent riots broke out in Ürümqi, Xinjiang. PRC officials said that a total of 197 people died. Two monorails of the Walt Disney World Monorail System collided at the Transportation & Ticket Center in Bay Lake, Florida, United States, killing one pilot and injuring seven others.
A public memorial service for Michael Jackson is held at Staples Center. It is watched by over 2.5 billion people worldwide.
Caspian Airlines Flight 7908, en route from Tehran, Iran, to Yerevan, Armenia crashes into the Jannatabad village in Qazvin Province; killing all 168 on board.
Iceland's national parliament, the Althingi, votes to pursue joining the EU.
Two bombs exploded separately at the JW Marriott and Ritz-Carlton Hotels in Jakarta, Indonesia, killing 9 people (including 2 suicide bombers) and injuring 53.
Amateur astronomer Anthony Wesley is the first to report that a new dark spot has developed on the planet Jupiter. This event would come to be known as the 2009 Jupiter impact event.
The longest total solar eclipse of the 21st century, lasting up to 6 minutes and 38.86 seconds (0.14 seconds shorter than 6 minutes and 39 seconds), occurs over parts of Asia and the Pacific Ocean.
The Islamic extremist group Boko Haram initiates an uprising in Bauchi State, Nigeria and quickly spreads throughout the northern part of the country.

Former President of the Philippines Corazon Aquino dies at the age of 76 of cardiopulmonary arrest after complications of colon cancer. A memorial service and funeral is scheduled for August 5. (Philippine Daily Inquirer)
Bolivia becomes the first South American country to declare the right of indigenous people to govern themselves.
Typhoon Morakot hits Taiwan, killing 673 and stranding more than 1,000 via the worst flooding on the island in half a century.
A small plane and a tour helicopter collide over the Hudson River in the United States. (CNN)
The United Kingdom imposes direct rule on the Turks and Caicos Islands after an inquiry that found evidence of government corruption.
At least five people are killed and 275 injured in a train crash near Yaoundé, Cameroon. (BBC) (Press TV)

2009 Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister helicopter crash. A helicopter carrying Y. S. Rajasekhara Reddy went missing in the Nallamala Forest area. It was later confirmed to have crashed with all five people including Reddy pronounced dead.
The Dubai Metro, the first urban train network in the Arabian Peninsula, officials opens.
China becomes the first country to succeed a completed clinical trial by a company for the 2009/H1N1 vaccine in the world during the swine flu pandemic.

WikiLeaks exposes the contents of Kaupthing Bank's internal documents prior to the Icelandic Financial Crisis. These documents showed suspicious amounts of money were loaned to bank owners, and debts being written off.
Korba chimney collapse: At least 45 workers are killed when lightning strikes a chimney under construction in Korba, Chhattisgarh, India, causing it to collapse.
Typhoon Ketsana, PAGASA Name: Ondoy, makes landfall in The Philippines, killing hundreds in Metro Manila and flooding in Huế, Vietnam.
At least 157 demonstrators are massacred by the Guinean military at the Stade du 28 Septembre during a protest against the government that came to power in a coup d'état the previous year.

A 7.6 Moment mag. scale</span>"}]]}'>Mw earthquake strikes Sumatra, Indonesia, with a maximum Mercalli intensity of VIII (Severe), leaving at least 1,115 people dead.
Paleontologists announce the discovery of an Ardipithecus ramidus fossil skeleton, deeming it the oldest remains of a human ancestor yet found.
Ireland holds a second referendum on the EU's Lisbon Treaty. The amendment is approved by the Irish electorate, having been rejected in the Lisbon I referendum held last year.
The International Olympic Committee awards Rio de Janeiro the right to host the 2016 Summer Olympics.
It is revealed the company Trafigura has been using a super-injunction to stop The Guardian from reporting about the 2006 Côte d'Ivoire toxic dumping incident, which Trafigura was responsible for.
British racing driver Jenson Button won his first Formula One World Championship, driving for Brawn GP at the Brazilian Grand Prix.
Susilo Bambang Yudhoyono is inaugurated for a second term as President of Indonesia.
WikiLeaks leaked the membership listing of a radical political group known as the British National Party.
Microsoft releases Windows 7 to all computers and laptops, including an edition for ATMs.
The 2009 Cataño oil refinery fire began after an explosion at the refinery in Bayamón, Puerto Rico.
The 2009 El Ayyat railway accident occurred in Giza, Egypt, when a passenger train derailed due to stoppage of animals on the train tracks. 50 people were killed and 30 people were injured.
Two suicide attacks in Baghdad, Iraq, kill 155 people and injure at least 721 people.
The Prime Minister of Belgium, Herman Van Rompuy, is designated the first permanent President of the European Council, a position he takes up on December 1, 2009.
The Czech Republic becomes the final member-state of the European Union to sign the Treaty of Lisbon, thereby permitting that document's initiation into European law.
Fourteen people are killed during the 2009 Fort Hood shooting.
Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 was released.
Having analyzed the data from the LCROSS lunar impact, NASA announces that it has found a "significant" quantity of water in the Moon's Cabeus crater.

In the Philippines, at least 58 people are abducted and killed in the province of Maguindanao, in what the Committee to Protect Journalists called the single deadliest attack on journalists in history.
The Avdhela Project, an Aromanian digital library and cultural initiative, is founded in Bucharest, Romania.
The Treaty of Lisbon comes into force.
Fire at the Lame Horse nightclub in Perm, Russia kills 156 people. The nightclub owner was sentenced to nearly ten years in prison.
18 - The UNFCCC's 2009 United Nations Climate Change Conference is held in Copenhagen, Denmark.
A series of attacks in Baghdad, Iraq kill at least 127 people and injure at least 448 more.
First flight of the Boeing 787 Dreamliner.
Astronomers discover GJ 1214 b, the first-known exoplanet on which water could exist.
Serbia applied for membership to the European Union.
A Nigerian terrorist plotted an attempted terrorist bombing of Northwest Airlines Flight 253 en route from Amsterdam to Detroit.
The tallest man-made structure to date, the Burj Khalifa in Dubai, United Arab Emirates, is officially opened.

The Togo national football team is attacked in Cabinda Province, Angola, and as a result withdraws from the Africa Cup of Nations. The attack was perpetrated by the FLEC, their first since the Angolan Civil War.
Religious violence erupts in Jos, Nigeria, which left scores dead, and many injured.
A 7.0-magnitude earthquake occurs in Haiti, devastating the nation's capital, Port-au-Prince.
Yemen declares an open war against the terrorist group al-Qaeda.
Honduras withdraws from ALBA.
The Chadian Civil War officially ends.
The longest annular solar eclipse of the 3rd millennium occurs.
North Caucasian Federal District was split from Southern Federal District by decree of Russian president Dmitry Medvedev.
Mahmoud Al-Mabhouh is assassinated in Dubai.
Ethiopian Airlines Flight 409 crashes into the Mediterranean shortly after take-off from Beirut-Rafic Hariri International Airport, killing all 90 people on board.
The sculpture L'Homme qui marche I by Alberto Giacometti sells in London for £65 million (US$103.7 million), setting a new world record for a work of art sold at auction.
The Australian government is hit by cyberattacks from freedom of expression activists, following recent Australian pornography restrictions.
28 - The 2010 Winter Olympics are held in Vancouver and Whistler, Canada.
Two trains collide in Halle, Belgium, killing 19 and injuring 171 people.

The president of Niger, Mamadou Tandja, is overthrown after a group of soldiers storms the presidential palace and form a ruling junta, the Supreme Council for the Restoration of Democracy headed by chef d'escadron Salou Djibo.
An 8.8-magnitude earthquake occurs in Chile, triggering a tsunami over the Pacific and killing at least 525. The earthquake is one of the largest in recorded history.

Pokémon HeartGold and SoulSilver Versions were released in North America. These are the highest rated games to date, with a user score of 9.1/10 on Metacritic, indicating "universal acclaim," and a critic score of 87.
The Kasubi Tombs, Uganda's only cultural World Heritage Site, are destroyed by fire.
Four-year-old Paulette Gebara Farah disappears from her family's home located in Huixquilucan, State of Mexico.

The ROKS Cheonan, a South Korean Navy ship carrying 104 personnel, sinks off the country's west coast, killing 46. In May, an independent investigation blames North Korea, which denies the allegations.
The first iPad is released.
Julian Assange leaks footage of a 2007 airstrike in Iraq titled "Collateral Murder" on the website WikiLeaks.
Kyrgyz President Kurmanbek Bakiyev flees the country amid fierce anti-government riots in the capital, Bishkek.
The president of Poland, Lech Kaczyński, is among 96 killed when their airplane crashes near Smolensk, Russia.
Volcanic ash from one of several eruptions beneath Mount Eyjafjallajökull, an ice cap in Iceland, begins to disrupt air traffic across northern and western Europe.

The Deepwater Horizon oil drilling platform explodes in the Gulf of Mexico, killing 11 workers. In the second round of the 2010 Hungarian parliamentary election the alliance of Fidesz lead by Viktor Orbán and the Christian Democratic People's Party (KDNP) wins enough seats to achieve a two-thirds supermajority in the legislature, beginning the 16-year second premiership of Viktor Orbán during

Standard & Poor's downgrades Greece's sovereign credit rating to junk 4 days after the activation of a €45-billion EU-IMF bailout, triggering the decline of stock markets worldwide and of the euro's value, and furthering a European sovereign debt crisis.
Expo 2010 is held in Shanghai, China.
First Greek bailout agreed
Nude, Green Leaves and Bust by Pablo Picasso sells in New York for US$106.5 million, setting another new world record for a work of art sold at auction.
The 2010 flash crash, a trillion-dollar stock market crash, occurs over 36 minutes, initiated by a series of automated trading programs in a feedback loop.
The 2010 United Kingdom general election results in a hung parliament, with the Conservative Party twenty seats short of a majority.
Scientists conducting the Neanderthal genome project announce that they have sequenced enough of the Neanderthal genome to suggest that Neanderthals and humans may have interbred.
Chile becomes the 31st member of the OECD.
The 2010 Philippine presidential election is held, with Benigno Aquino III elected as Philippine President.
Afriqiyah Airways Flight 771 crashes at runway at Tripoli International Airport in Libya, killing 103 of the 104 people on board.
Following the 6 May United Kingdom general election, the Conservative and Liberal Democrat parties agree to form a coalition government, the UK's first since the Second World War.
Protests in Bangkok, Thailand, end with a bloody military crackdown, killing 91 and injuring more than 2,100.
Five paintings worth €100 million are stolen from the Musée d'Art Moderne de la Ville de Paris.
Scientists announced that they have created a functional synthetic genome.
Inter Milan beats Bayern München 2-0 in the 2010 Champions League Final at the Santiago Bernabéu.
Air India Express Flight 812 overshoots the runway at Mangalore International Airport in India, killing 158 and leaving 8 survivors.
29 - The Eurovision Song Contest 2010 takes place in Oslo, Norway, and is won by German entrant Lena with the song "Satellite".
the 2010 Ahmadiyya mosques massacre in Lahore, Punjab, Pakistan, killed 94 people during Friday prayers at two mosques.
Nine activists are killed in a clash with soldiers when Israeli Navy forces raid and capture a flotilla of ships attempting to break the Gaza blockade.
The Chicago Blackhawks win their first Stanley Cup since 1961.
14 - Ethnic riots in Kyrgyzstan between Kyrgyz and Uzbeks result in the deaths of hundreds.
July 11 - The 2010 FIFA World Cup was held in South Africa and was won by Spain.
Wedding of Victoria, Crown Princess of Sweden, and Daniel Westling
25 - A tennis match between Nicolas Mahut and John Isner at the Wimbledon Championships, becomes the longest tennis match in history.
FIA appointed Pirelli as official tyre partner and supplier for Formula One from 2011 season onwards.
Julia Gillard is elected unopposed in a Labor Party leadership ballot and sworn in as the first female prime minister of Australia following the resignation of Kevin Rudd.
The first 24-hour flight by a solar-powered plane is completed by the Solar Impulse.
Microsoft ends extended support for Windows 2000.
First (test) Instagram posts made by co-developers Mike Krieger and Kevin Systrom in San Francisco; the service launches publicly on October 6.
Slovenia becomes the 32nd member of the OECD.

WikiLeaks, an online publisher of anonymous, covert, and classified material, leaks to the public over 90,000 internal reports about the United States-led involvement in the War in Afghanistan from 2004 to 2010.
Airblue Flight 202 crashes near Islamabad, Pakistan, killing all 152 people on board.

PDVAL affair, also known as the Pudreval affair, political scandal in Venezuela where tons of rotten food supplies were found torrent, which imported during Hugo Chávez's government through subsidies of state-owned enterprise PDVAL.
Heavy monsoon rains begin to cause widespread flooding in the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province of Pakistan. Over 1,600 are killed, and more than one million are displaced by the floods.
The World Health Organization declares the H1N1 influenza pandemic over, saying worldwide flu activity has returned to typical seasonal patterns.
AIRES Flight 8250, a Boeing 737-700, crashed on landing at San Andrés, Colombia, killing two.
2010 Australian federal election: Julia Gillard's Labor government is re-elected, narrowly defeating the Liberal/National Coalition led by Tony Abbott.
The Manila hostage crisis occurred near the Quirino Grandstand in Manila, Philippines killing 9 people, including the perpetrator, while injuring 9 others.

A 7.1 magnitude earthquake rocks Christchurch, New Zealand causing large amounts of damage but no direct fatalities. Israel becomes the 33rd member of the OECD.

Anonymous initiates Operation Payback, a coordinated cyberattack on multiple corporations, law firms, and politicians over the banning of file-sharing websites such as LimeWire and The Pirate Bay and also the politicians and financial institutions against WikiLeaks, a whistleblower website.
Građevni kombinat 'Međimurje' from Čakovec, one of the largest Croatian construction and civil engineering companies (with more than 8,000 employees in 1980s), ceased to exist
14 - 2010 Commonwealth Games takes place in Delhi, India.
Germany makes final reparation payment for World War I.
Instagram was launched.
The Netherlands Antilles are dissolved, with the islands being split up and given a new constitutional status.
Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu says that he will extend the settlement freeze if the Palestinian leadership recognizes Israel as a Jewish state. The Palestinians quickly reject the offer.

The Finnish Yle TV2 channel's Ajankohtainen kakkonen current affairs program featured controversial Homoilta episode (literally "gay night"), which led to the resignation of almost 50,000 Finns from the Evangelical Lutheran Church.

The 2010 Iraq War Documents leak occurs, being deemed the biggest US government leak in history. WikiLeaks being responsible for revealing 391832 documents concerning the 2003 Iraq War which revealed approximately 60% of the Iraqi deaths were civilian casualties, the Iraq War body count project show
The International Space Station surpasses the record for the longest continuous human occupation of space, having been continuously inhabited since November 2, 2000 (3641 days).

In preparation for the Seoul summit, finance ministers of the G-20 agree to reform the International Monetary Fund and shift 6% of the voting shares to developing nations and countries with emerging markets.
An earthquake and consequent tsunami off the coast of Sumatra, Indonesia, kills over 400 people and leaves hundreds missing.

Repeated eruptions of Mount Merapi volcano in Central Java, Indonesia, and accompanying pyroclastic flows of scalding gas, pumice, and volcanic ash descending the erupting volcano kill 353 people and force hundreds of thousands of residents to evacuate.
Dilma Rousseff is elected, becoming the first (and, so far, the only) female president from Brazil.
Expo 2010 concludes in Shanghai, China.

2010 United States elections were held on Tuesday, November 2, 2010, in the middle of Democratic President Barack Obama's first term. Republicans ended unified Democratic control of Congress and the presidency by winning a majority in the House of Representatives.
Qantas Flight 32 suffers an engine failure requiring an emergency landing in Singapore.
Aero Caribbean Flight 883 crashes in central Cuba, killing all 68 people on board.
12 - The G-20 summit is held in Seoul, South Korea. Korea becomes the first non-G8 nation to host a G-20 leaders summit.
Burmese opposition politician Aung San Suu Kyi is released from her house arrest after being incarcerated since 1989.
Sebastian Vettel became the youngest F1 Champion after a 4 way championship fight.
Researchers at CERN trap 38 antihydrogen atoms for a sixth of a second, marking the first time in history that humans have trapped antimatter.
Participants of the 2010 NATO Lisbon summit issue the Lisbon Summit Declaration.
Eurozone countries agree to a rescue package for the Republic of Ireland from the European Financial Stability Facility in response to the country's financial crisis.

North Korea shells Yeonpyeong Island, prompting a military response by South Korea. The incident causes an escalation of tension on the Korean Peninsula and prompts widespread international condemnation. The United Nations declares it to be one of the most serious incidents since the end of the Kore
WikiLeaks releases a collection of more than 250,000 American diplomatic cables, including 100,000 marked "secret" or "confidential".

December 10 - The 2010 United Nations Climate Change Conference is held in Cancún, Mexico. Formally referred to as the 16th session of the Conference of the Parties of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (COP 16), it serves too as the 6th meeting of the Parties to the Kyoto Pro

The European Union agree to an €85 billion rescue deal for Ireland from the European Financial Stability Facility, the International Monetary Fund and bilateral loans from the United Kingdom, Denmark and Sweden.
Comet Hale Bopp was found again around 30.7 AU away from the Sun. The previous time the Comet was found was in April 1997.
Estonia becomes the 34th member of the OECD.

After 25 years on CNN, Larry King Live airs its final episode. Contemporary reporting noted that King had recorded more than 6,000 programs for the network and that he was reported to be listed in the Guinness World Records for hosting the longest-running show with the same host in the same network
The attempted suicide of Mohamed Bouazizi, a street vendor in Tunisia, triggers the Tunisian Revolution and the wider Arab Spring throughout the Arab world.
The first total lunar eclipse to occur on the day of the Northern winter solstice and Southern summer solstice since 1638 takes place.
Estonia officially adopts the Euro currency and becomes the 17th Eurozone country.
Flight 348 with 134 occupants, operated by Metrojet, catches fire while taxiing out for take-off. Three people are killed and 43 are injured, four critically, from smoke inhalation or burns.
A bomb explodes as Coptic Christians in Alexandria, Egypt leave a new year service, killing 23 people.

Tunisian street vendor Mohamed Bouazizi dies after setting himself on fire a month earlier, sparking anti-government protests in Tunisia and later other Arab nations. These protests become known collectively as the Arab Spring.
Internet vigilante group Anonymous launches DoS attacks on government websites of Syria, Tunisia, Bahrain, Egypt, Libya, and Jordan in response to the Arab Spring protests.

A Bangladeshi teenage girl Felani Khatun, was shot dead by the Indian Border Security Force (BSF) on the Anantapur border area under Phulbari upazila in Kurigram. Her body was hanging from the fence for four and half hours. Global human rights organizations, including the media, became protesters.
Iran Air Flight 277 crashes near Orumiyeh in the northeast of the country, killing 78 people.
The Tunisian government falls after a month of increasingly violent protests; President Zine El Abidine Ben Ali flees to Saudi Arabia after 23 years in power.
The result of the South Sudanese independence referendum, 2011 is in favour of independence, paving the way for the creation of the new state in July.
37 people are killed and more than 180 others are wounded in a bombing at Domodedovo International Airport in Moscow, Russia.
The 2011 Egyptian revolution begins.
Within Ursa Minor, H1504+65, a white dwarf with the hottest known surface temperature in the universe at 200,000 K, was documented.
Friday of anger (Egyptian revolution of 2011). Protestors clash with security forces which resulted in over 600 protestors estimated dead and several police stations were raided.
Manx2 Flight 7100, a Fairchild Metro III, crashes on its third attempt at landing at Cork airport, Ireland from Belfast. Six of the twelve passengers and crew are killed.
Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak resigns after widespread protests calling for his departure, leaving control of Egypt in the hands of the military, until a general election can be held.
The Day of Rage in Bahrain begins, which marks the first day of the 2011 Bahraini uprising.
The First Libyan Civil War starts.
April 2 - The 2011 Cricket World Cup is held in India, Bangladesh, and Sri Lanka with India defeating Sri Lanka in the final.
March 14 - Uncertainty over Libyan oil output causes crude oil prices to rise 20% over a two-week period following the Arab Spring, causing the 2011 energy crisis.

A 6.3 magnitude earthquake strikes Christchurch, in what becomes New Zealand's third-deadliest natural disaster. 185 people are killed, many ESL students within the CTV Building, and the city centre and 10,000 homes are destroyed. Many foreign search and rescue workers respond to the event.
The Nintendo 3DS has its first release in Japan, following later releases in Europe on March 25, North America on March 27, and Australia on March 31.
Egyptian protestors storm the State Security headquarters in the Nasr City district of Cairo.
Civil uprising phase of the Syrian Civil War is triggered when 15 youths in Daraa are arrested for scrawling graffiti on their school wall denouncing the regime of President Bashar al-Assad.

A 9.1-magnitude earthquake and subsequent tsunami hit the east of Japan, killing 19,759 people and leaving another 2,553 missing. Tsunami warnings are issued in 50 countries and territories. Emergencies are declared at four nuclear power plants affected by the quake. As a result of the March 11 eart

Egypt’s Ministry of Interior dissolves the widely feared and hated State Security Investigations Service accused of human rights abuses and announced the establishment of the new National Security Agency will replace it and take over its internal security duties.
Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa, King of Bahrain, declares a three-month state of emergency as troops from the Gulf Co-operation Council are sent to quell the civil unrest.

Protests breakout across Syria demanding democratic reforms, resignation of President Bashar al-Assad, and release of those imprisoned for the March 6 Daraa protest. The government responds by killing hundreds of protesters and laying siege to various cities, beginning the Syrian Civil War, which la
The United Nations Security Council votes 10-0 to create a no-fly zone over Libya in response to allegations of government aggression against civilians.

In light of continuing attacks on Libyan rebels by forces in support of leader Muammar Gaddafi, military intervention authorized under UNSCR 1973 begins as French fighter jets make reconnaissance flights over Libya.
The Israel Defense Forces use their Iron Dome missile system to successfully intercept a BM-21 Grad launched from Gaza, marking the first short-range missile intercept ever.

Former Ivorian President Laurent Gbagbo is arrested in his home in Abidjan by supporters of elected President Alassane Ouattara, with support from French forces; this effectively ends the 2010-11 Ivorian crisis and civil war.

The Mexican town of Cherán is taken over by vigilantes in response to abuses from the local drug cartel. The new government is strongly focused on crime reduction and preserving the local environment.
The 2011 PlayStation Network outage begins, becoming one of the largest data breaches ever recorded, and exposing personal data from 77 million accounts on the platform. The outage lasted 23 days.
